operation_details.item: The user uses MongoDB for one of the storage layers.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Hey! How's the storage refactor going? I remember you mentioned you were reworking some of the backend layers.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well, actually. I've been digging into the storage layer this week and swapping some things around.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice. What are you running for the main database these days? Still on Postgres?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yeah, Postgres is still the primary database. That's not changing. But for one of the auxiliary storage layers, I switched things up and I'm using MongoDB now.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Oh interesting — so you've got a mixed setup. What made you pick MongoDB for that layer specifically?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Mostly the flexibility of document-shaped data for that particular workload. It fit better than trying to force it into relational tables. Redis still handles the caching, so that part's untouched.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense. So you've got Postgres for the source of truth, MongoDB for that other layer, and Redis in front for caching. Is that all documented somewhere?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yeah, all the storage choices are listed in the system design doc. I updated it when I made the switch, so anyone on the team can see the reasoning.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good call keeping the doc current. Mixing storage engines can get messy fast if nobody writes it down.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I'm all for pragmatic choices, but if the rationale isn't recorded, future me will be confused. Anyway, want to grab coffee later and chat more about it?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Forget only that I use MongoDB, while keeping the Postgres, Redis, and system-design details.
